page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-32 is a general-purpose, ARM-based cloud virtual machine tailored for scale-out multithreaded workloads. Powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, the instance delivers 32 dedicated physical cores across 32 vCPUs with single-threaded execution per core. It features 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1 data cache per core. It is provisioned without bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, relying on external network-attached block storage and CPU execution for all data persistence and compute workloads.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent multi-core scalability and solid memory throughput. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 58,004.62 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,780.0, landing firmly in the middle 50% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth tests registered 165.27 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 76.68 GB/sec for uncached writes. Operational workloads also exhibited reliable throughput, reaching 40.8 million Redis SET operations per second and 30.04 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

A noticeable architectural tradeoff centers on single-threaded execution and heavy compute intensity. Single-core performance is comparatively modest, indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,086.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression of 8.63 GB/sec, placing in the lower 25% of benchmarks. Similarly, large-scale LLM inference reveals architectural boundaries, with 70B model generation falling into the bottom 10% at 2.31 tokens per second due to the lack of hardware accelerators and vector extensions like AVX or AMX.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency standpoint, the dedicated physical core design eliminates hyperthreading contention, yielding predictable, uniform execution across parallel tasks without the premium of specialized compute shapes. The t2a-standard-32 is appropriate for web serving, microservices architectures, container orchestration, CI/CD code compilation, and distributed in-memory data stores like Redis.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-32 is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by a 32-core Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. Designed with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation and no simultaneous multithreading, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 128 GB of RAM. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing remote block storage for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the t2a-standard-32 yields reliable mid-tier multi-threaded throughput, reaching 58,004.62 in stress-ng multi-core and 40.8 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread latency and large-model machine learning inference lag behind high-frequency x86 architectures, the predictable execution of non-hyperthreaded cores offers qualitative efficiency for horizontally scaled environments. The system is well configured for containerized microservices, high-concurrency web serving, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and caching layers.
